subject: PD-8 runtime boundary between baseline and isolate
claim: The isolate repository can stand up its own MCP gateway, from its own source, under its own compose project, with mounts resolving inside its own tree — and GET /identity can name which of the two repositories answered.
not_claimed: Nothing about multi-peer ZDO delivery, motion capture, netcode behaviour, or the image promotion lane. This is a runtime boundary result only.

revisions.note: isolate's working tree was dirty during the run because these fixes were uncommitted at probe time. /identity reported source_dirty=true, which is the gate working: it declined to attest a clean revision it could not stand behind.

defects_found_before_any_change.summary: isolate/docker/valheim-lab.compose.yml declared name: comfy-valheim-lab — the live lab project — and AUTONOMOUS_ROOT/COMFY_ROOT had no defaults, so unset values rendered the world mounts as blank-rooted absolute paths (/state/server/data). docker compose exited 0 with warnings only, meaning the documented Phase 2 command would have adopted the running server and recreated it against an empty world directory.
defects_found_before_any_change.evidence: docker compose config --format json, rendered before any edit

defects_found_before_any_change.summary: gateway_identity() hardcoded project="baseline", and source_root is /workspace inside any container built from network/mcp/Dockerfile. /identity — the endpoint PD-8 nominates as the contract boundary — was structurally unable to distinguish the two repositories.

isolate's gateway service set none of the six COMFY_MCP_* provenance variables and mounted only the valheim,inference providers, while the identity gate requires the workbench provider plus non-empty revision/dirty/image.

contracts/api-contract.json did not describe the implementation beside it: /healthz declared 'status' but returns ok/gateway; /identity declared 'port' but returns listen_port/published_port; transport declared default_port 8721, which is baseline's companion container host publish, not the kernel default of 8720.
defects_found_before_any_change.status: fixed, and now enforced by test

defects_found_before_any_change.summary: isolate's test suite was red 2/11: DISTRIBUTION_SCOPE named network/mod/ComfyNetworkSense/README.md and Lumberjacks/docs/workbench/tools, which PD-8 deliberately left in baseline. AGENTS.md forbids publishing images with tests failing, so the promotion lane was blocked.

Pre-existing on the baseline side and NOT introduced here: the identity gate is red against the live 8721 endpoint with source_revision_missing,source_dirty_missing. Root cause is that the companion compose passes ${...:-unknown} and env_value() maps the literal 'unknown' to null by design; nobody exports the real values at launch.
defects_found_before_any_change.status: root-caused, NOT fixed — out of scope, see follow_ups

follow_ups.summary: isolate has no git remote. PD-8's promotion lane ('publish versioned container images, consume them in baseline') is not reachable: baseline can only rebuild from a sibling directory, which is the coupling PD-8 exists to remove. Until there is a remote and a published tag, the two repos are duplicated source, not a boundary.

D6 — baseline's companion dev-mcp launch does not export LUMBERJACKS_COMPANION_SOURCE_REVISION/BRANCH/DIRTY, so the live 8721 endpoint fails its own identity gate. The fix is a launcher that stamps git provenance, the same shape as isolate's Start-IsolateLab.ps1.
The compose file remains duplicated between the repos with no drift guard. Deciding which copy is authoritative — or deleting one — is unresolved.

Live lab telemetry reports players=Durracktu,Tugcorp with peer_count=0. Determine whether player names are retained after disconnect, and if so, whether Test-LocalLabQuiescence should treat that as quiescent.

third_blocker_NEW_DEFECT.severity: blocking for the alpha client-pull lane
third_blocker_NEW_DEFECT.summary: Release m7-c10b-20260807-r42 cannot be installed by the headless Companion update lane. The install was refused on OMEN with HTTP 400 package_personalized_config_forbidden, detail BepInEx/config/djcdevelopment.valheim.comfynetworksense.cfg.
third_blocker_NEW_DEFECT.the_guard_is_correct: Game.Companion/Program.cs:999 refuses any package carrying that entry, because the Gateway stores only a credential hash after install and overwriting the file would erase the one copy of the raw access key the client owns. Nothing was forced past it.
third_blocker_NEW_DEFECT.root_cause: Two halves of the same codebase disagree about which artifact the headless lane receives. Game.Companion/Program.cs:842 fetches GET /api/v0/valheim/modpack/package, which SteamEnrollmentEndpoints.cs:76 serves as the raw template via Results.File(File.OpenRead(release.package_file)) — unmodified. The config-stripping build, ModPackBuilder.BuildConfigPreservingUpdatePack, exists and is correct, but is only reachable through /join/update/steam-callback (SteamEnrollmentEndpoints.cs:138), which requires Steam OpenID in a browser. Install-I5LatestModpack.ps1 documents itself as deliberately avoiding that flow. So the headless update lane and the config-preserving pack builder never meet.
third_blocker_NEW_DEFECT.why_it_surfaced_only_now: Confirmed by inspecting the stored templates in artifacts/modpacks/. m31-motionphase-20260724-r1, m32-workbench-20260802-r1, and m32-watchdog-20260802-r1 are each 33 entries with NO personalized config entry. m7-c10b-20260807-r42 is also 33 entries but DOES carry it. Today's cut swapped one file, and that single change is what the installer guard refuses. The three prior releases installed headlessly because their templates happened to lack the entry.
third_blocker_NEW_DEFECT.the_real_tension: New-AlphaModpack.ps1:95-102 stages the config entry deliberately, because the /join first-install lane REQUIRES it — ModPackBuilder.BuildPersonalizedPack throws if the template has no such entry. So the template must carry it for first install and must not carry it for headless update. One artifact cannot satisfy both; the update lane has to strip, which is exactly what BuildConfigPreservingUpdatePack does and exactly what no headless route calls.
third_blocker_NEW_DEFECT.proposed_fix: Serve the stripped pack on a Consumer-gated headless route (e.g. GET /api/v0/valheim/modpack/package/update running TryBuildConfigPreservingUpdatePack) and point Game.Companion/Program.cs:842 at it. Requires rebuilding both the Gateway and Companion images. Not attempted — outside the authorized scope, and guessing at it would have meant rebuilding two images on a hypothesis.
third_blocker_NEW_DEFECT.verification_of_the_evidence: The downloaded package hashed to c5ee672f26dedad7e20e7063c38235fe34dd8d1b3d8bcae9e24bc86ab959821b at 1085425 bytes, matching the manifest exactly, so the entry list above is the artifact the gateway actually serves and not a stale local copy.
